subject: Daz
fact: Daz believes a corpse does not lie and that everything it knows is written on it, to be read by the observer.
source_quote: There is a particular comfort in a corpse. It does not lie. It does not run a counter-play. Everything it knows is written on it, and all I have to do is read.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz thinks the killer had time and was not in a rush, because the blows were precise and there was no blood spray.
source_quote: The blows had been precise. Too precise, too close together, for a man fighting back. No spray across the room — no blood pressure left to throw it. Janussi had been dead before his chest was opened. Whoever did this had not been in a rush. He had not been trying to kill. He had been desecrating a corpse at his leisure, with nowhere to be.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz notices clotted blood under the nose and smeared bloodstains on the right sleeve of the tunic, indicating Janussi was writing when killed.
source_quote: Clotted blood under the nose. Smeared bloodstains on the right sleeve of the tunic — the *right* sleeve, the working hand.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz realizes the black substance on Janussi’s finger and lip is not ink, because it is darker than the ink in the well.
source_quote: The tip of his left forefinger was blackened. Not blue. Darker than blue. And the same dark smudge sat dead-center on his lower lip. ... No. Not ink. That was the entire point of the long look — not that the finger was stained, but that the stain was *wrong*.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz suspects the black substance is poison because of its unusual darkness and the way it was transferred from page to finger to lip.
source_quote: Do we think this black stuff might be poisonous? I thought it the likeliest answer.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz understands that the chip in Janussi’s tooth came from falling face-first, not from the murder itself.
source_quote: He had fallen forward. Face-first. Chipped the tooth on the way down.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz believes the killer rolled Janussi onto his back after death to remove his heart.
source_quote: And then the patient hands arriving after, in no hurry at all, rolling the body and opening the chest to make certain he stayed gone.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz suspects the killer took only one sapphire and one parchment because they needed exactly that one thing, not because they were greedy.
source_quote: Somebody is trying to build a sapphire spell... a spell that requires a sapphire. ... Whoever did this came in, took one sapphire, and walked past a king's ransom.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz notices three circular impacts and holes in the armchair and identifies them as darts of pure force.
source_quote: Three circular impacts, horsehair stuffing scattered, two holes punched clean through the chair back.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum remembers that bruising cannot form on a corpse because there is no living tissue to swell.
source_quote: Bruising doesn't form on a corpse; there's no living tissue to swell.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum realizes the broken nose happened before death, because the bruising was formed while blood was still moving.
source_quote: The bruising around the broken nose held its color, dark and settled, the way bruising only sits when blood was still moving when it formed.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum notices the impression of a chain on Janussi’s neck and identifies two broken lead links as evidence of a locket or necklace being torn off.
source_quote: The impression of a chain on the back and sides, and beneath it two broken lead links. Something had hung there, and someone had torn it off him.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum suspects the tobacco pipe was used to mask the smell of poison.
source_quote: tobacco smoke would hide the smell of poison. Of course it would.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum believes the safe was not forced open because the lock was undamaged, meaning the killer had the combination or no need for it.
source_quote: The safe. A box of metal as wide as a man's reach, sunk into the tower wall, its door standing open. ... Open, but undamaged. No forced entry.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum observes that the treasure in the safe was untouched, indicating the killer was not motivated by greed.
source_quote: Still inside the safe were four sealed pouches, each with its sapphire — and beside them a figurine of a raven, a potion of supreme healing, another of water breathing, five diamonds each worth a fortune, a heap of platinum and gold, a small treasury left untouched.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum thinks the statue of A'lai Aivenmore was knocked over accidentally by the scholar who discovered the body.
source_quote: The statue had simply fallen, it turned out. The Great Reader A'lai Aivenmore had knocked it over in shock when he found the body at dawn.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum feels a quiet sorrow at the image of a clerk dying mid-sentence in his own library.
source_quote: I noted that and felt something I didn't examine too closely — a clerk dying mid-sentence in his own library. There are worse exits.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin mutters that he has the second-worst eye for detail in the room, implying he knows he’s bad at observation.
source_quote: Thorin muttered something about having the second-worst eye for detail in the room.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is afraid the candle on the statue might be magically alive and could cause danger.
source_quote: I don't want it to wake up and attack us... I've had, you know, had bad experiences.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin believes the darts aimed at the chair were not meant for Janussi, since he bore no such marks.
source_quote: those darts never miss their mark, Thorin pointed out, and the man bore no such marks.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir wonders if the black substance on Janussi’s finger is like Dumbledore’s style, suggesting he’s making a pop-culture reference.
source_quote: Like, Dumbledore style? Or, like—

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir suggests Glabbagool might have ingested the black substance and could help identify it.
source_quote: Wouldn't Glabbagool have ingested, like, all sorts of different kinds of materials and poisons and goo in the Underdark?

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir realizes the bruise on Janussi’s nose must have occurred before death because corpses cannot bruise.
source_quote: Grygum, you've got the healer's eye, right? How does bruising work if he's dead? Like, I would assume you don't really. ... You don't — you don't bruise after you're dead.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir observes that the blue ink on *The Discoveries* was the last thing Janussi wrote, and that it came after ink on *The Golden Ass*.
source_quote: The blue ink on *The Discoveries* had been laid down after the blue ink on another book. *The Golden Ass.*

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is curious about what Janussi was writing in his final unguarded moment, believing the room reads better when you ask what a man was doing then.
source_quote: I'm curious… trying to understand what he was writing at the time of death. The room reads better when you ask what a man was doing in his last unguarded minute than when you ask who he was.

subject: The missing locket
fact: The locket or necklace taken from Janussi’s neck is unidentified, but its removal suggests personal or symbolic significance.
source_quote: Something had hung there, and someone had torn it off him. A locket, a necklace — gone, snapped at the chain.

subject: The missing sapphire and parchment
fact: The killer took only one sapphire and one parchment, indicating a targeted goal rather than random theft.
source_quote: Somebody is trying to build a sapphire spell, a spell that requires a sapphire.

subject: The darts at the chair
fact: The three darts of pure force fired at the chair have no clear motive, and their purpose remains unexplained.
source_quote: Why would you loose three darts of force at a chair?

subject: The black substance
fact: The black substance is unknown but potent enough that even Glabbagool, an ooze that has eaten the Underdark, cannot identify it.
source_quote: Even his failure carried a verdict: there was *something* about the black, something that mattered. When even a creature that has eaten the Underdark can't place a poison, you've learned the poison is worth being afraid of.
